item.title: Large-scale monitoring of Earth’s tidal response on the deep seafloor using fiber-optic sensing
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04189-1

Distributed Acoustic Sensing enables sensitive, continuous monitoring of Earth tides in the deep sea, with potential applications to constraining the elastic and mechanical properties of the upper crust in offshore regions and calibrating ocean tide models, according to an analysis of a 53-km offshore telecom fiber-optic cable near Toulon, southern France.
item.dc:title: Large-scale monitoring of Earth’s tidal response on the deep seafloor using fiber-optic sensing

item.title: Atmospheric dissolved organic carbon deposition closes a missing link in the global terrestrial carbon cycle
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04209-0

Canopy interception dominates atmospheric deposition of dissolved organic carbon, according to a process-explicit reconstruction of dissolved organic carbon utilizing carbon isotope data and machine learning.
item.dc:title: Atmospheric dissolved organic carbon deposition closes a missing link in the global terrestrial carbon cycle

item.title: Contrasting ecological patterns across deglaciating Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords revealed by soft-sediment benthic assemblages
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04216-1

Soft-sediment benthic assemblages vary among fjords and with glacier proximity, with diversity increasing toward fjord mouths while biomass and density show fjord-specific patterns across glacier-distance gradients in three Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords.
item.dc:title: Contrasting ecological patterns across deglaciating Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords revealed by soft-sediment benthic assemblages

item.title: High-resolution mapping reveals trade-offs among tea production, food security and biodiversity conservation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04153-z

Tea production shows uneven trade-offs among economic returns, food security, and biodiversity across major producing countries, with China achieving the strongest balance and Kenya underperforming in all three, based on 10-m satellite mapping and cross-country sustainability assessments.
item.dc:title: High-resolution mapping reveals trade-offs among tea production, food security and biodiversity conservation

item.title: Sea level rise and subsidence compound flood risks on the century-old Treasure Island
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04158-8

Treasure Island is subsiding by 5–11 millimeters per year and sliding by up to 6 millimeters per year, sea-level rise is projected to become the main driver of flood risk by 2030, with substantial inland inundation risk by 2050, according to satellite data, geomechanical modeling, and deep learning.
item.dc:title: Sea level rise and subsidence compound flood risks on the century-old Treasure Island

item.title: Climate-driven functional and structural decoupling in urban agglomeration forest networks for ecosystem adaptive management
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04184-6

Climate change drives divergent and often mismatched shifts in forest function and connectivity across the Pearl River Delta, requiring response-specific management, based on network simulations integrating functional diversity and landscape structure under three climate pathways from 2010 to 2100.
item.dc:title: Climate-driven functional and structural decoupling in urban agglomeration forest networks for ecosystem adaptive management
